newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power steady on warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power steady on warmer weather.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. were steady Tuesday, supported by outlook of warmer weather next week, brokers and traders said.
"There'll be some warmer weather in mid-80's (Fahrenheit) degrees in the Northeast next week," said one Houston trader.
Most participants said a brief power outage Monday afternoon in parts of upstate New York and Long Island had little market impact today.
The blackout was caused by a failure in a circuit breaker on a 345 kilovolt power line in the Catskills region of New York.
New York Power Pool (NYPP), which oversees the reliability of electricity deliveries within the state, said the transmission system statewide returned to normal operation Monday night
In NYPP, firm, peak electricity prices for next-day delivery were quoted at $23.00-$24.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $22.00-$24.00 late last weekend.
Next-day NYPP power for off-peak hours was assessed in the $18.00-$22.50 range.
September NYPP electricity for peak delivery was valued at $21.00-$21.60 and off-peak in the $16.00 area.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), firm, peak power for Wednesday delivery was discussed at $25.00-$27.00, near unchanged from levels late last weekend.
Next-day NEPOOL prices for off-peak hours were pegged at $18.00-$22.50.
